label: TMUA 2023 · Paper 2 · Question 8
knowledgePattern: Exhaust the possible locations of a right angle in a triangle-dividing cut
solution:
A straight cut producing two triangles must run from a vertex to an interior point of the opposite side. A new right angle can be at that point, or at the cut vertex; the two untouched original angles are not right.

For an acute triangle, each of the three altitudes meets the opposite side internally and gives a valid cut. A cut cannot create a right angle at an acute vertex, so there are exactly three.

For an obtuse triangle, only the altitude from the obtuse vertex has its foot inside the opposite side. A cut from either acute vertex cannot create a right angle there. At the obtuse vertex, however, one internal cut can be drawn perpendicular to either of its adjacent sides, giving two more cuts. Each perpendicular ray lies strictly within the obtuse angle and meets the opposite side internally.

These three cuts are distinct: the two vertex-perpendicular cuts differ from one another, and an altitude cannot also give a right angle at its starting vertex, since that would put two right angles in one triangle. Thus every permitted triangle has exactly three cuts. Statement III only: answer D.

hints.title: Decide where a cut can go
hints.body: A straight cut that makes two triangles must start at a vertex and end inside the opposite side. Sketch one.
hints.recap: Use triangle sides and vertices to check the shapes made by a cut.
hints.pitfall: A new right angle could be at either end of the cut.
hints.pause: Mark the possible locations of the right angle.

recall.reminder: Use triangle sides and vertices to check the shapes made by a cut.

hints.title: Try an acute triangle
hints.body: Draw cuts perpendicular to opposite sides. Also consider whether a cut can split an acute angle into a right angle and another positive angle.
hints.recap: An acute triangle has all its angles less than ninety degrees.
hints.pitfall: Only a cut inside the original triangle is allowed.
hints.pause: Count the valid cuts and explain why your list is complete.

recall.reminder: An acute triangle has all its angles less than ninety degrees.

hints.title: Now try an obtuse triangle
hints.body: Check which perpendiculars to opposite sides stay inside. At the obtuse vertex, also try a cut perpendicular to either adjacent side.
hints.recap: An exhaustive count separates the possible cases and checks that none are missed or counted twice.
hints.pitfall: Do not count a perpendicular meeting only an extension of a side. Check that proposed cuts are distinct.
hints.pause: Count all valid cuts in this case, then decide which statements are possible.
